source: QZ issue #1018 physical Life Fitness treadmill Android HCI capture
evidenceTier: upstream hardware-observed evidence; not FitBridge tier H
why: Plan section 11 requires observed timing as part of a hardware evidence record, and Phase 6 had
none archived. It also indexes the continuity hazards inside the existing measurement corpus
(life_fitness_issue_1018_ftms_treadmill_capture.json) by sequence, so a fusion or parser test
can reach them by name instead of by eyeballing 221 packets.
Sequence numbers here are the same 1-based numbering that fixture uses.

notificationCadence.note: nominally 1 Hz and not actually 1 Hz. A freshness or staleness bound derived from an assumed exact 1000 ms would false-positive on this machine.

duplicateNotifications.note: byte-identical repeat of the previous notification, including the elapsed-time counter. Naive cumulative accumulation double-counts distance and energy here.

flagTransitions.note: flag word changes mid-stream, so field offsets shift between consecutive notifications on the same characteristic
flag word changes mid-stream, so field offsets shift between consecutive notifications on the same characteristic

continuityHazards.elapsedTimeRestart: Session 2 restarts the elapsed-time counter at 1 while total distance and expended energy also restart at 0. A cumulative-metric carry across a reconnect must treat the counter reset as a new session rather than as a rollover.
continuityHazards.sentinelValues: Ramp angle is 0x7FFF and negative elevation gain is 0x7FFF in every packet; energy per hour is 0xFFFF and energy per minute is 0xFF until the machine has a value. These are the SIG not-available sentinels and must be surfaced as absent, never as 3276.7 degrees or 65535 kcal/h.

privacy: Timing, link parameters and structural anomaly indices only. No addresses, device name, absolute timestamps or profile data. The one retained packet is FTMS Treadmill Data, which carries no identifying values.
